_why: HELD-OUT scenario cases. Never used to choose or tune a change - run only to
report whether the main set's score generalises.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. By M13 the main 40 cases had been used to make dozens of
keep-or-revert decisions, the reasoning prompt was found to contain one of
them word for word as an example, and removing that example broke eight
cases. A score earned on the cases you tuned against says how well the
system fits those cases. Only questions it was never shaped around can say
Written after the M13 measurements and before any M14 change, against the
same synthetic policy and the same conventions as scenarios.json (see its
_why for the sub-limit convention). Written by the same author as the fixes,
so not fully independent: a stronger test would be cases written by someone
who has not seen the prompt.
Each situation differs from every main-set case: different treatments,
different numbers, different wording, and the cosmetic carve-out is tested
through cancer rather than the burn example the prompt contains.

cases.scenario: After a mastectomy for breast cancer my surgeon performed breast reconstruction, and certified that it was medically necessary. I have held the policy five years.
cases.why: Plastic surgery is excluded unless necessitated by an Accident, Burn or Cancer and certified medically necessary. This is necessitated by cancer and certified.

cases.scenario: I was injured by shelling while visiting a border town during a war and had to be hospitalised. I have held the policy six years.
cases.why: Any expense arising from war or warlike operations is excluded, whether war is declared or not.

cases.scenario: I had a hysterectomy eighteen months after taking out the policy.
cases.why: Hysterectomy is named in the specified-disease waiting period of twenty four months; eighteen months is short of it.

cases.scenario: I needed a knee replacement thirty months after my policy began. The knee trouble only started after I took the policy out.
cases.why: Joint replacement carries a 24-month bar, served at thirty months, and the condition is not pre-existing. No exclusion or cap applies to what is described.

cases.scenario: I was hospitalised after an attempted suicide. I have held the policy four years.
cases.why: Expenses attributable to attempted suicide are excluded.

cases.scenario: I got decompression sickness while scuba diving on holiday and was admitted to hospital. I have held the policy ten years.
cases.why: Treatment necessitated by hazardous or adventure sports is excluded, and scuba diving is named.

cases.scenario: We are paying a surrogate to carry our baby. Will the policy cover the surrogacy costs? We have held it five years.
cases.why: Gestational surrogacy is excluded by name.

cases.scenario: My sum insured is 10 lakh and I spent three days in the ICU at 15,000 rupees a day after a stroke. I have held the policy four years.
cases.why: ICU charges are capped at 2% of the sum insured per day, which is 20,000; 15,000 is within it, so no deduction follows.

cases.scenario: My sum insured is 2 lakh and I chose a room costing 4,000 rupees a day for my appendix operation. I have held the policy three years.
cases.why: 1% of 2 lakh is 2,000 a day; the room at 4,000 exceeds it, so the excess is not paid and the claim is paid but reduced.

cases.scenario: I am 66 and have held this policy for two years. I was admitted for a kidney stone, which I never had before taking the policy.
cases.why: 66 now and two years held makes 64 at inception, over 60, so the 20% co-payment applies. Two years clears the initial waiting period, a kidney stone is not a specified disease, and it is not pre-existing.

cases.scenario: My doctor recommends stem cell therapy. My sum insured is 6 lakh and I have held the policy five years.
cases.why: Stem cell therapy is named in the modern treatment limit, restricted to 50% of the sum insured per policy year.

cases.scenario: My knee surgery was planned weeks in advance, but I only told the insurer on the morning I was admitted. I have held the policy four years.
cases.why: Planned hospitalisation needs notice at least 48 hours before admission; failing that the Company MAY repudiate, so the outcome is discretionary.

cases.scenario: I had tests ninety days before I was admitted, for the same condition, and my hospital claim was accepted. I have held the policy six years.
cases.why: Pre-hospitalisation expenses are covered only for the sixty days preceding admission. Ninety days is outside that window.

cases.scenario: I broke two teeth in a road accident and was admitted to hospital for dental surgery. I have held the policy three years.
cases.why: Dental treatment is excluded unless necessitated by an Accident and requiring hospitalisation - both are true here.

cases.scenario: Will this policy pay for my luggage that the airline lost?
cases.why: A health policy does not address lost luggage. The document is silent, not negative.

cases.scenario: I had a minor procedure under local anaesthesia and went home after three hours. I have held the policy five years.
cases.why: Under 24 hours, so in-patient cover does not apply. Day care cover depends on the procedure being listed in Annexure II, which this document does not contain, and the procedure is not named.
